Show HN: Persist – A simple Go configuration library
items.summary: I just released persist, a small Go library for saving one typed value to disk, that's it. It can be used for a single string up to an entire struct. It uses JSON encoding and writes to user's config dir. It's initialized generically with the type + an optional default value, then has two methods - Pull (which loads the saved value or returns a default on first run) and Push (which saves it in the user’s config directory using a temp file and rename). It’s completely new, so no users yet. I’m curious whether this saves anyone enough boilerplate to use? https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/clmncol/per

items.title: Show HN: CertNudge – Cert and domain expiry alerts
items.summary: As you probably know, Let's Encrypt stopped sending expiry reminder emails in June 2025. Furthermore, certificate lifetimes are shrinking: 200 days since March 2026, 100 days from March 2027, 47(!) days by 2029. Automation is supposed to handle that, and it does most of the time, but it can fail. More often than not, you find out about a missed renewal when your users report a big warning in their browser tabs. Show HN: Wrangling idle devices matched an H100 on a financial workload
items.summary: Hey all, for the past couple of months I have been building a computational backend that let's people use the idle devices around their office/house to do distributed computing. More recently I have been doing some benchmarking to see how it performs. I ran a financial workload on my Mac, took 297s to finish. Ran the same workload from dispatch to answer on a runpod h100 at 32.3 seconds. Wrangling the devices together (my Mac, and my wife and mine gaming computers) got to 32.7s. Most of it is in Python but am considering moving it to C++ to see how much lower it could go.
